title: Training Note: Credit Base for a Vehicle Removed from a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
When a vehicle comes off a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, the credit base of its vehicle removal credit follows how the removed vehicle was charged during the term.

## The rule

The removed vehicle's addition is its latest vehicle addition entry in the policy's transaction history, by effective date.

| How the removed vehicle was charged | Credit base |
|---|---|
| Its addition carries an additional premium entry of the current term | The charge written on that entry times the credit days, divided by the days that charge was written for: the unearned share of what was actually charged |
| It was added during the term with a premium effect, but no additional premium entry was written for it | Nil: nothing was charged |
| Otherwise | The full-term drop times the credit days, divided by the days of the removal's term |

**Days the charge was written for.** These are the calendar days to the term expiration date, counted from one of two dates:
- from the addition's effective date, where the addition was recorded no more calendar days after that effective date than the package's newly acquired additional report days;
- otherwise, from the date the addition was recorded.

| Package | Newly acquired additional report days |
|---|---|
| Cardinal Auto Essential | 14 |
| Cardinal Auto Basic | 14 |
| Cardinal Auto Standard | 14 |
| Cardinal Auto Plus | 14 |
| Cardinal Auto Preferred | 30 |
| Cardinal Auto Premier | 30 |

"Added during the term" means the addition's effective date is on or after the term effective date. "With a premium effect" means the addition entry shows a premium effect other than none.

## Questions answered

**Hypothetical, Cardinal Auto Plus.** A vehicle added effective 2 March 2026 and recorded 10 March (8 days, within 14) carries an additional premium entry of 200.00 for the term 1 January to 1 July 2026. It is removed with 61 credit days. What is the credit base?
The charge was written for the 121 days from 2 March to 1 July. The credit base is 200.00 times 61 divided by 121, which is 100.8264…, carried unrounded.

**The same addition, recorded on 20 March (18 days, beyond 14)?**
The charge was written for the 103 days from 20 March. The credit base is 200.00 times 61 divided by 103.

**The same vehicle added during the term with a premium effect, but no additional premium entry exists for its addition?**
The credit base is nil.

**A vehicle that was on the schedule from before the term began?**
It falls under "otherwise": the full-term drop on the removal entry times the credit days, divided by the days of the removal's term.
